title: Staged deploy guardrails and automatic rollback tooling for canaries and percent ramps
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Define and implement a robust set of guardrails and upgrade tooling for staged deployments across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. The scope covers: canary deployments, percentage traffic ramps, feature-flag based rollouts, health/golden metric gates, and automated rollback orchestration that works with both cloud-hosted endpoints and on-prem/private clusters. The goal is to reduce release blast radius while enabling predictable, auditable rollouts and safe LTS upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: A canary launch flow is available that routes 1% traffic to a canary revision and evaluates health against golden metrics for a configurable window.
A percent-ramp policy can be defined (examples: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated pauses and manual-override hooks.
Automatic rollback triggers if any critical gate breaches (p99 latency +15%, error rate +300% relative, SLI saturation) within the evaluation window.
Feature-flag integration allows toggling rollout scope by org, region, or customer tier without redeploying code.
Upgrade tooling provides a dry-run mode that simulates traffic shifts and produces a rollout plan report (including estimated risk and time-to-full-ramp).
All rollout decisions and gate evaluations are recorded in the Console audit trail and surfaced in a dedicated rollout dashboard.
End-to-end e2e tests and a chaos test run validate rollback behavior in a staging cluster.
rollout_plan: Phase A: Implement lightweight canary router for Hosted API (edge proxy config + runtime flag). Start with 1% for 30 minutes.
Phase B: Add percent-ramp controller that reads a RampPolicy CRD and advances on success criteria or halts on failure.
Phase C: Integrate golden metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error ratio, CPU/GPU saturation, KV cache hit rate, and a custom QA regression score.
Phase D: Wire feature flag targeting into rollout controller so feature flags can gate behavior for Dedicated and Private customers.
Phase E: Implement auto-rollback orchestration: snapshot previous revision, shift traffic back to safe revision, send alerts and open incident ticket template.
Phase F: Provide CLI and Console UI for creating RampPolicy, viewing live gate status, and forcing rollback/continue.
technical_notes: Gate evaluation runs every 1 minute during canary window; uses rolling baselines to avoid noisy spikes for low-volume customers.
Threshold examples: latency p95 must not increase by more than 10% relative to baseline; error rate must not exceed baseline + 0.5 percentage points or 3x (whichever smaller).
Auto-rollback should require two independent gate breaches within a configurable window (default 2 consecutive minutes) to avoid flapping during transient spikes.
For on-prem/Private, the rollout controller runs in passive mode and emits a recommended action; optional operator agent applies traffic changes where direct control is unavailable.
We will reuse existing tracing and metrics pipelines (Prometheus + tracing) and add a lightweight evaluation service that can run as a sidecar or control-plane job.
State model: RampPolicy (string ID), Stage objects with percentage, duration, success_criteria, rollback_criteria. Represented as YAML/JSON for CLI and Console import.
Security: rollout actions are gated by RBAC scopes; audit entries must include user, policy snapshot, and metric deltas.
decision_log: 2025-01-22: Decided on staged percent ramps (1/5/20/50/100) as default with policy overrides per-project (approved by Release Eng).
2025-01-29: Chose a two-breach confirmation rule for auto-rollback to reduce false positives (agreed with SRE).
2025-02-03: For Private deployments, initial release exposes a recommended-mode rollout controller; full automated control deferred pending legal approval.
risks: False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks for low-volume customers — mitigated by relative thresholds and minimum sample sizes.
Operator confusion when Console shows 'recommended' vs 'applied' in Private — mitigated by clear UI labels and walkthrough docs.
Rollback may be slow for large stateful revisions (DB migrations) — releases with destructive schema changes must be flagged and excluded from auto-rollback flows.
Dependency on metrics pipeline latency could delay gate evaluations; add health checks for metrics freshness and fallbacks to manual pause.
test_plan: Unit tests for RampPolicy parsing and state transitions.
Integration test: simulate 1k rps with injected regression and assert automatic rollback within 5 minutes.
Chaos test in staging: induce 30% CPU spike on canary nodes to validate pause/rollback behavior.
End-to-end demo: product+SRE run showing canary -> ramp -> rollback -> audit trail in Console.
